transcript: Tonight I saw JOB at Soho Playhouse and it was one of the most compelling theater pieces I've seen in a while. This 80 minute play is a therapy session for a high- strung millennial woman working in tech who's been placed on leave after having a bit of a mental health crisis gone viral. The therapist is much older and is more of a hippie and a lot of the play teases out this dissonance between their ideologies around work and the internet. The vulture review of this play describes it like a Black Mirror episode and I would totally agree. The way it unfolds is extremely compelling and well paced and has a twist that I will not spoil, you need to be in the room to experience it. It’s also phenomenally acted, my eyes were absolutely glued to the stage the entire time. I really hope it comes back to New York after its already sold out run ends in mid October because it's a play that I think is not only thrilling to see but also to talk about. I got a rush ticket on TodayTix so if you can, go see it. Do note though it contains some heavy and potentially triggering content. And if you have seen it please sound off in the comments with any thoughts I'm super curious. I went alone and I wish I hadn't. With that, another program for my collection
